section_2_20_candidate_orbits_symbolic.label: CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF -- recomputed at full phase-level precision
section_2_20_candidate_orbits_symbolic.regularity_finding: each of orbit 91's own 5 hexagons has exactly 5 attaching candidate orbits -- a uniform 5x5=25 structure, with 5 orbits (42,78,90,93,126) each appearing twice at different qualifying phases

required_registration_ordering_lemma.statement: for orbit q to serve as a direct FZ1 witness, its very first-ever touch must land exactly on the qualifying phase. If the first touch lands elsewhere, direct FZ1 for q is permanently foreclosed. A delayed route remains: reaching the qualifying phase later via Z2 fired while continuously resident in q since opening -- departure requires an R-kind re-entry, which is R2 itself, terminal, never intermediate
required_registration_ordering_lemma.consequence: component change via any candidate q requires either exactly one event (first touch is the qualifying phase) or exactly two events (open elsewhere, then uninterrupted Z2 completion)

section_2_20_candidate_orbits_symbolic.grouping: by attachment hexagon only (the 5 groups in attachment_table) -- no continuation equivalence inferred or claimed among orbits sharing a group

section_3_five_hub_touching_orbits.label: CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF -- derived forbidden-pattern lemma

derived_lemma.statement: for any q in {96,120,126,128,129}, realizing C_R1 -> q -> C_H requires visiting two structurally distinct phases of q. The second touch must be a Z2 fired while continuously resident in q since it was opened; departure forces the only route back to be an R-kind re-entry, which is R2 itself, terminal.
derived_lemma.status: PROVED, necessary condition, not an impossibility result

section_3_five_hub_touching_orbits.shortcut_ruled_out: R2 cannot simultaneously create and benefit from the merge -- target_a_recognizer's same_component check is computed from the incidence forest BEFORE the R2 transition fires (established four rounds ago), so the merge must already exist prior to R2

section_4_144_bound_revisited.label: CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF with an explicit self-correction

self_correction.what_was_retracted: the earlier citation of '(720-visited) decreases by exactly 6 per move' as a general law
self_correction.why: on rechecking, this was Round 54's own empirical finding on one specific 64-edge sample of one branch's ancestry, not a first-principles derivation. Re-derived from extend()'s own mechanics: each call advances visited_count by exactly 1 window regardless of move weight; weight governs F/S/H deltas, not window count. A macro edge of rotation length ell plus one joint visits ell+1 windows, which varies with ell (state-dependent) -- no general reason for this to equal 6 uniformly, and three-rounds-ago data already recorded rotation lengths 0,1,2,3 at different points on these branches

what_remains_valid.orbit_pigeonhole: Z3 requires a fresh orbit (om[q]==0); ORBIT_COUNT=144 total orbits confirmed directly from source; sound and unconditional, needs no window-counting mechanism

section_4_144_bound_revisited.gap_exposed_by_the_task: the original framing conflated Z3-EVENT-COUNT (144, bounded) with TOTAL-MOVE-COUNT or search EFFORT before FZ1 could occur (unbounded by this argument) -- between successive Z3s, arbitrarily many Z2/rotation moves and, separately, arbitrarily many rejected collision attempts (which consume no window budget at all) can occur

strongest_valid_replacement.bound_1: at most 144 Z3 events fire in any single branch's history (orbit-pigeonhole, solid)
strongest_valid_replacement.bound_2: at most HEX_COUNT x N = 120 x 6 = 720 genuine successful literal single-window-advancing moves of any kind fire in any single branch's history (window-budget pigeonhole, re-derived from extend()/ExactState source this round, not inherited from an empirical citation)
strongest_valid_replacement.bound_3_none_derived: no bound is derived on the number of rejected/colliding candidate attempts -- the quantity search-tree 'expansion' counts actually measure, empirically large relative to genuine moves per prior rounds' pilot data

section_4_144_bound_revisited.key_distinction: neither bound says anything about WHEN FZ1 occurs relative to overall search cost -- they bound branch CONTENT, not discovery EFFORT
